identity_admission.proof: Both loop-health routes derive tenant scope from verified JWT claims and environment scope from verified claims or the exact deployed PANTHEON_ENV; a missing tenant returns 403 tenant_scope, a cross-tenant request returns 403 tenant_scope, and a cross-environment request returns 403 environment_scope.

pre_deploy.environment: active local Pantheon Postgres controller store on localhost:15432
pre_deploy.terminal_readback: Controller records were written and read back through the real Postgres store rather than a fake: concurrent success/failure/heartbeat/backlog writers were replayed against the live database, fenced-lease renewal and stale-generation rejection were observed after takeover, desired/actual JSONB observations round-tripped with source and checked_at intact, and same-loop rows stayed isolated across tenant and environment keys. No hosted deployment readback is claimed by this lane.

proof: One controller identity is the composite (tenant_id, environment, loop_id); a repeated write for the same identity merges into the current row inside a transaction-scoped advisory lock plus current-row FOR UPDATE and a single UPSERT, so a duplicate observation cannot create a second row or resurrect a stale snapshot.
evidence_refs is a stable deduplicating union and truth_level advances by monotonic rank, so replaying the same evidence reference or a lower truth level is a no-op rather than a regression.

test_concurrent_partial_updates_preserve_monotonic_fields shows that interleaved success, failure, heartbeat, and backlog writers cannot lose a newer field: monotonic event timestamps never move backwards and independent fields are preserved.

test_projector_reports_later_failure_as_unhealthy and test_projector_does_not_manufacture_evidence_or_healthy_expired_lease keep a later failure and an expired lease visible as unhealthy instead of degrading into a false healthy claim; test_loop_health_registry_only_lists_all_loops_without_live_claim keeps a catalog-only loop from reporting live truth.

Desired-state presence and downstream actual state are persisted only as explicit observations carrying source and checked_at; test_projector_stale_heartbeat_and_query_text_do_not_manufacture_actual_state confirms that query text alone stays unobserved and non-authoritative.

test_loop_health_service_store_overlays_controller_health_and_events and test_loop_health_rejects_runtime_record_from_wrong_controller_identity show that the BFF correlates a projected loop only with the controller record whose identity matches the authenticated lookup key, and discards a store result whose tenant_id or environment differs.

test_normal_writes_renew_fence_and_stale_generation_is_rejected exercises real controller-generation replacement against the live Postgres store: every normal write renews a future generation-specific lease, an expired lease is taken over under the same serialized transaction key with a rotated opaque lease_token, and the previous generation's writes are rejected afterwards, so a controller that restarts or is replaced cannot corrupt the record it no longer owns.

test_lease_safety_and_stale_heartbeats and test_store_crud_and_validation reload persisted controller rows from Postgres after the writing session ends and recover the exact identity, lease, timestamp, and observation fields.

Each controller update is a single Postgres transaction holding the identity advisory lock, so a failed merge rolls back completely and leaves the previously durable record as the authoritative truth; no partially applied controller state is published.
This lane grants no deployment, allocation, runtime-control, catalog-maturity, or live-capital mutation authority, so no compensating financial action exists to perform.

environment_boundary.proof: Only merged Pantheon dev integration and the bounded local Postgres controller store were exercised. Environment scope comes from verified claims or the exact deployed PANTHEON_ENV, and a cross-environment lookup returns 403 environment_scope; hosted activation is not claimed.

mfa.proof: This control-plane read and controller-store lane changes no interactive operator authentication or MFA policy.

no_live_capital.proof: The controller record, its projector, and the loop-health reads carry no broker, allocation, or capital authority, and no live-capital path was enabled or widened.

rbac.proof: Loop truth reads require a verified identity; an unauthenticated or tenant-less request fails closed with 403 tenant_scope rather than falling back to an environment default, and no new write authority was granted to the read plane.

tenant_isolation.proof: test_loop_health_database_lookup_uses_authenticated_tenant_and_environment plus test_store_isolates_same_loop_by_tenant_and_environment show exact tenant_id and environment filtering for both Postgres and file-fallback records, an explicit X-Tenant-Id must remain within the allowed tenant claims, and the BFF discards any store result whose returned scope differs from the authenticated lookup key.

two_person_approval.proof: Owner and reviewer remain distinct: Codex2 independently reviewed and approved candidate 147495e6bb323f15e004909ee9e48f454a325e7b with reviewer evidence commit d1854c512eef24de21b0f859a9f7a07f6d4d9dee, and owner-of-record Claude performed closeout without re-approving its own work.

acceptance.statement: Concurrent success, failure, heartbeat, and backlog updates cannot lose newer fields.
Normal writes renew fenced leases and stale writers are rejected.
The BFF projects desired-state presence and authoritative downstream actual state as explicit observations, never from query text alone.
Controller truth lookup is scoped by authenticated tenant and environment.
A reusable conformance suite covers all required controller fields for all twelve canonical loops.
The independent reviewer decision is durable, cites the exact reviewed candidate, and is preserved unchanged through owner closeout.
